fieldsRead.text: Applied Physics combines physical theory, mathematical models and experiments to understand natural phenomena and develop technologies. The curriculum includes mechanics, electromagnetism, optics, quantum and statistical physics, materials and laboratory research.

The UCR options offer related mathematical modelling, computation, physical-system investigation and energy or resource applications. The first emphasizes algorithms and computational methods alongside physical measurement; the second adds more Earth science, geochemistry and resource laboratory work. Neither reproduces the complete Applied Physics discipline.
Elective selections require approval and must satisfy the programme’s level and non-overlap rules.

Required 15 EC final project. Entry requires at least 120 EC, all compulsory first-year study, at least 110 EC of core and ITEC study, completed Advanced Computational and Experimental Skills, and laboratory safety training. The ordinary Q4 start follows the required taught study; other permitted project timing remains subject to these conditions.

Laboratory safety training is required before practical participation and adds no credits. The same safety condition applies to data acquisition, experimental automation, advanced experimental skills and the final project.
Requires completion of previously offered study embedding communication, cooperation, planning and organisation skills.

20 EC of approved elective study in year 2 and 25 EC in year 3. At least 30 EC must be intermediate or advanced, including 15 EC advanced. Content may not overlap. Submit the complete 180 EC plan for approval after earning at least 90 EC; changes also need approval.

Engineering Ethics and Engineering for Society each carry 5 EC. At least five Studium Generale activities are required within ITEC. Personal and professional development and other first- and second-year challenges are embedded; MyFuture activities with a combined value of seven add no credits.

The UCR options combine mathematical and computational models with physical-system investigation and sustainable energy or resource applications. They include some wave, mechanical, thermal and materials work, but do not reproduce the full mechanics, electromagnetism, optics, thermodynamics, transport, quantum and condensed-matter sequence, cumulative physics laboratories or compulsory Applied Physics final project.

selectedDescriptionsRead.ACCPPDE101: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.
selectedDescriptionsRead.DISGATE101: Introduces programming and computer science. Covers structured programming, data constructs, testing, debugging and object‑oriented programming with Python, and develops computational problem‑solving skills.
selectedDescriptionsRead.DISARIN212: Focuses on mathematics of decision‑making, covering topics in discrete mathematics such as logic, patterns and structures, with applications to computer science and algorithm construction.
selectedDescriptionsRead.ENSGATE101: Introduces sustainability through planetary boundaries and scientific tools for understanding human impacts on Earth systems. Students interpret graphs and uncertainty, build simple dynamic models, and study chemical and physical principles relevant to climate, energy and materials. A laboratory project makes and tests starch-based biopolymers.
selectedDescriptionsRead.DISGATE102: Mathematical Methods develops foundational techniques in differentiation, integration, complex numbers and differential equations. Students solve problems analytically and with Mathematica. A project implements, analyses and adapts a dynamic model, requiring interpretation of its behaviour and computational results.
selectedDescriptionsRead.ENSGATE201: Develops physical-science foundations for sustainability through waves, chemistry and materials science. Reflective work and a project apply these topics to analysing greenwashing.
selectedDescriptionsRead.DISDATA111: Develops foundational skills in data visualization, cleaning and manipulation. Explores spatial and text data and includes hands‑on work with datasets from various disciplines.
selectedDescriptionsRead.DISARIN311: Optimization Methods in AI studies search and optimisation for rational agents. Topics include uninformed and heuristic search, local and global optimisation, adversarial search, constraint satisfaction, linear programming and discrete optimisation. Laboratory exercises and projects develop algorithm implementation, evaluation and experimental investigation of small intelligent systems.
selectedDescriptionsRead.DISCOMP211: Introduces computer networks and operating systems. Covers how the internet works and the role of an OS in resource management and application support.
selectedDescriptionsRead.DISCOMP311: Teaches design and analysis of algorithms and data structures, emphasizing performance analysis and focusing on prominent algorithms and data structures.
selectedDescriptionsRead.DISMATH211: Linear Algebra studies systems of equations, matrices, vectors, linear transformations and vector spaces. Students examine eigenvalues, orthogonality, least-squares approximation, quadratic forms and singular value decomposition. Applications include discrete signals, difference equations, Markov chains, dynamical systems, graphics and principal component analysis, with Mathematica supporting analytical problem-solving.
selectedDescriptionsRead.DISDATA212: Image Processing & Computer Vision studies how digital images are represented, processed and interpreted to recognise structures and objects. Topics include colour, image statistics, filtering, segmentation, feature detection, tracking and object classification. Practical work uses Python and OpenCV to develop and benchmark an image-recognition pipeline on previously unseen images.
selectedDescriptionsRead.DISMATH213: Introduces numerical methods such as root‑finding, interpolation, numerical differentiation and integration and solving differential equations. Emphasises algorithm accuracy, stability and efficiency and uses computer algebra software.
selectedDescriptionsRead.DISMATH312: Linear Systems studies signals and linear time-invariant systems. Students examine impulse and frequency responses, convolution, Fourier series and transforms, and the Laplace and Z transforms, including continuous-time and discrete-time representations.
selectedDescriptionsRead.DISDATA312: Covers computational problems in robotics. Includes forward and inverse kinematics, motion planning, collision avoidance and robotic grasping and manipulation.
selectedDescriptionsRead.DISMATH314: Provides a foundation in mathematical statistics. Covers probability theory, discrete and continuous distributions, sampling, parameter estimation and simulation; uses computer algebra software to develop theoretical understanding and practical skills.
selectedDescriptionsRead.DISDATA211: Machine Learning introduces methods for understanding data and making predictions, including linear regression, classification, resampling, shrinkage, tree-based methods, support vector machines and clustering. Real-world examples illustrate the methods, their strengths and limitations.
selectedDescriptionsRead.DISARIN211: Decision-making in AI examines how intelligent agents make decisions under uncertainty. Students study probability, Bayesian networks, temporal models, expected utility, Markov decision processes, partial observability and bandit problems. Multi-agent decisions and probabilistic programming extend the analysis, supported by equations, numerical examples and scientific papers.
selectedDescriptionsRead.ENSSUST111: Focuses on drivers and impacts of anthropogenic climate change on sea level, ocean acidification, ecology and society. Discusses adaptation and mitigation solutions, including renewable energy systems, carbon storage and climate‑adaptive planning, and examines climate governance and justice.
selectedDescriptionsRead.DISMATH214: Extends elementary calculus to multiple dimensions and differential equations, including complex‑valued functions. Uses computer algebra software to deepen analytical skills for science and data analysis applications.
selectedDescriptionsRead.DISDATA311: Neural Networks & Deep Learning combines theory with practical Python, Keras and TensorFlow implementations. Students build and train networks, study backpropagation, regularisation and model evaluation, and apply deep learning to computer vision, time series and text, including transformers. Projects investigate prediction problems and report experimental results.
selectedDescriptionsRead.ENSSUST311: Teaches assessment of energy usage patterns and strategies for reducing consumption or transitioning to cleaner energy. Explores solar, wind and bioenergy solutions and includes technical and economic analysis; students deliver a report and presentation to a partner company.
selectedDescriptionsRead.ENSENVI213: Explores interactions among biosphere, hydrosphere, lithosphere and atmosphere. Teaches system modelling, uses proxies and isotope tracers to study past and future climates and includes a field trip focused on greenhouse gas pathways.
selectedDescriptionsRead.ENSENVI111: Introduces Earth Science by focusing on interactions among the deep earth, lithosphere and hydrosphere. Highlights key cycles shaping Earth’s surface and includes indoor/outdoor labs and a multi‑day field excursion.
selectedDescriptionsRead.ENSENVI212: Explores soils and aquifers through fieldwork and lab analyses. Covers soil formation, properties, health and remediation and investigates mapping aquifers for geothermal energy, coastal defence and freshwater resource assessment.
selectedDescriptionsRead.ENSENVI311: Examines chemical and biological controls on interactions among water, minerals, rocks and soils. Topics include equilibrium, speciation, redox chemistry, adsorption, weathering and biomineralisation. Laboratory work, geochemical modelling and an environmental project connect these processes to contaminant behaviour, wastewater treatment, remediation and resource recovery.
selectedDescriptionsRead.ENSDELT311: Examines strategies and technologies towards a circular economy. Explores resource security and stewardship, develops lab skills and inorganic chemistry knowledge, and connects to themes at the Delta Climate Center.
selectedDescriptionsRead.ENSENVI312: Provides in‑depth geoscience research into resource and environmental challenges such as nuclear waste storage, geothermal energy and CO₂ capture. Students conduct literature reviews and produce class reports for presentation to a professional conference.
